label: copy phase: input e, about to output h (recalling the bigram e->h)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or <DEL>), almost always when the fed-back input is e (96% of activation mass; about 4% on input h). The strongest activations come when the original sequence had e immediately followed by h, so the model takes e as input and must output h. Top examples are all ...e h... sequences at activation 0.9-1.0 of max. Activation is weak or absent when e h sits at the very start of the sequence (recall_idx 1, e at step L+1). The predicate e->h with recall_idx>=2 has dev precision 0.89 and covers 66% of activation mass and 87% of the top quartile. The rest is a long tail of weak activations (mostly under 0.2 of max) on copy-phase e inputs followed by other tokens; these fire on only about 5% of such steps, and neither repeated e nor the presence of h elsewhere explains them. It does not fire on e in the original phase, on first occurrences of a token, or on other inputs, apart from weak h->h steps just after e h.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=e (+8.43), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+4.50), in_tok=e (+4.14), phase=2 & out_tok=h (+3.96), out_tok=h (+3.72), in_tok=h (+3.14). Lower it: out_tok=a (-3.71), out_tok=w (-3.17), out_tok=p (-3.00), orig4=- (-2.97).
